newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung says has no plan to join Communist Party.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung says has no plan to join Communist Party.

text.p: Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa, a wealthy former shipping magnate, says he has no plan to join the Communist Party, a prerequisite for those holding power in China, now the region's ruler.
Tung also said the all-powerful Chinese party did not plan to get involved in politics of the bustling capitalist enclave, which Britain handed back to China on Monday night.
He made the remarks in an interview in the Chinese-language newspaper Hong Kong Economic Journal, published on the third day of Chinese rule in Hong Kong.
Appointed by Beijing to Hong Kong's top job, Tung also paid tribute to the party, saying it had made taken great strides since it opened China to economic modernisation in the 1970s.
Hong Kong is to enjoy a high degree of autonomy under the "one country, two systems" formula espoused by China's late leader Deng Xiaoping for the next 50 years.
"I have no plans of becoming a Communist Party member," Hong Kong's Chief Executive told the Journal.
"The Communist Party has no plans of joining the political arena, otherwise, we would not need the 'one country, two systems' formula," he said.
He also said Beijing was determined to let Hong Kong run itself, except in areas of defence and foreign affairs.
"China's rulers are very determined to realise the 'one country, two systems', and so are Hong Kong people."
Tung, nonetheless, paid tribute to China's Communist Party.
"Over the last 19 years since China opened up, the country has taken off in many areas and the Communist Party has led the country to good results."
